Let \(A=k[h,s]\), and define \(\sigma\in \operatorname{Aut}_k(A)\) by
\[
\sigma(h)=\zeta h,\qquad \sigma(s)=\zeta^2s.
\]
Then
\[
xa=\sigma(a)x,\qquad ya=\sigma^{-1}(a)y\qquad (a\in A).
\]

The defining relations give a PBW-type normal form
\[
R=\bigoplus_{i,j\ge 0} A x^i y^j
\]
as a left \(A\)-module, because the only nontrivial overlap is resolved by replacing \(yx\) with \(xy+c\), where
\[
c=(\zeta^{-1}-1)h+(\zeta^{-2}-1)s+(\zeta^{-3}-1)hs+hs^2.
\]

If \(z\in Z(R)\), then \(z\) must commute with both \(h\) and \(s\). A monomial \(a x^i y^j\) has weight \(\sigma^{i-j}\) against \(A\), so commuting with \(h,s\) forces
\[
i-j\equiv 0\pmod 5.
\]
Thus every central element is a sum of homogeneous terms of degrees divisible by \(5\).

Now set
\[
t=xy.
\]
Since \(xy\) commutes with \(A\), the degree \(0\) part is \(A[t]\). Also
\[
xt=(t-\sigma(c))x.
\]
So a degree \(0\) central element \(F\in A[t]\) must satisfy
\[
F=\alpha(F),
\]
where \(\alpha|_A=\sigma\) and \(\alpha(t)=t-\sigma(c)\). Since
\[
\sum_{r=0}^4 \sigma^r(c)=5hs^2,
\]
we get
\[
\alpha^5(t)=t-5hs^2.
\]
Because \(\operatorname{char} k=0\) and \(hs^2\neq 0\), no nonconstant polynomial in \(t\) is fixed by this translation. Hence the degree \(0\) central elements are exactly
\[
A^\sigma=\{f(h,s): f(\zeta h,\zeta^2s)=f(h,s)\}.
\]

For positive degree \(5m\), a homogeneous central element has the form \(F x^{5m}\). Commuting with \(x\) forces \(F\in A^\sigma\). But
\[
[y,x^{5m}]
=\left(\sum_{r=0}^{5m-1}\sigma^r(c)\right)x^{5m-1}
=5m\,hs^2\,x^{5m-1}\neq 0,
\]
so \(F x^{5m}\) cannot commute with \(y\) unless \(F=0\). The negative-degree case with \(y^{5m}\) is analogous. Therefore the center is precisely \(A^\sigma\).

Finally, \(A^\sigma\) is generated by the invariant monomials whose exponent pairs \((a,b)\) satisfy
\[
a+2b\equiv 0\pmod 5.
\]
This semigroup is generated by
\[
(5,0),\ (0,5),\ (3,1),\ (1,2),
\]
so
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[h^5,\ s^5,\ h^3s,\ hs^2]}.
\]
